abstract_sentences: At 57 qubits, standard conformal intervals calibrated on the public labels contain 41 of 45 held-out labels but the reference (DMRG) value of the staggered magnetization at 0 of the 45 training couplings and at 0 of the 4 test couplings, where the cubic model misses it by 2.28 to 3.73 times the tolerance.

Calibrated instead on the 18 labels that the published energy and site magnetizations certify to within half the tolerance (Jz = 4.3 to 6.0), intervals built from the exact energy bounds were narrower than the tolerance in 200 of 200 random splits (0.56 to 0.86 of it) and contained the reference value in 1000 of 1000 cases, for both declared models; the true value varies by only 0.30 of the tolerance over that range, so this shows that the guarantee survives the learner and its calibration, not that a hard function was learned.
abstract_sentence_alternative: With all 45 public training labels in the calibration set, no learner using a constant-width score can return a guaranteed interval narrower than 5.35 times the tolerance at the test couplings (57 qubits; 4.65 at 115).
